title: She said "Let's get off." It was NOT my stop 🚇 내립시다 #learnkorean
caption:
내립시다 (nae-rip-si-da) looks like "let's get off" — 내리다 (get off) + the "let's" ending.

But on a packed subway or bus, people shout it to mean "I'm getting off — coming through!" It's not an invitation. Don't follow them out. 😅

What you can say when it's your stop:
잠시만요, 내릴게요. (jam-si-man-yo, nae-ril-ge-yo) — Excuse me, I'm getting off.

Shorter: 내릴게요! (nae-ril-ge-yo) — Getting off!

alt: A needle-felted Seoul subway car, packed. A felt lady pushes toward the doors shouting 내립시다! (nae-rip-si-da). The coral felt mascot Mongle hears "Let's get off!" and follows her out. On the platform she walks away without looking back. The door chime sounds, Mongle rushes back, the doors shut and the train leaves. Mongle is alone: "It was not my stop." What she meant: "I'm getting off!" Next time, you say: 잠시만요, 내릴게요 — "Excuse me, I'm getting off." Last shot: Mongle alone on a bench in the empty station, practicing the phrase. Next train: 8 min.
